claims.claim: Value describes how light or dark a tone appears. Contrast is the difference between elements; strong contrast can attract attention, though placement and context also matter. Composition organises visual elements into relationships. Balance concerns distribution of visual weight and can be symmetrical or asymmetrical. A simple value study using a few tones makes large patterns easier to inspect before adding detail. There is no universal rule that every image needs a central focal point.

locators.limitations: Not universal criteria for artistic worth
